Directed by Ben Cookson and stars Noah Schnapp, Jean Reno and Anjelica Huston.

programme.title: Spear
programme.desc: Acclaimed Artistic Director and Choreographer Stephen Page brings Bangarra Dance Theatre's outstanding dance work SPEAR to the screen. Striking and original, Page weaves story through dance to deliver an extraordinary cinematic experience in his feature film debut.

programme.title: Summerland
programme.desc: During World War Two, a reclusive Englishwoman finds her life up-ended when a young evacuee from the London Blitz is left in her care. Initially resolving to be rid of him, she finds herself opening her heart in this moving story of womanhood, love and friendship. Directed by Jessica Swale and stars Gemma Arterton, Gugu Mbatha-Raw and Lucas Bond.

programme.title: Madison
programme.desc: At the centre of the family story is 13-year-old protagonist Madison, for whom cycle racing means just everything! programme.title: The Way Ahead
programme.desc: A mismatched collection of conscripted civilians find training tough under Lieutenant Jim Perry and Sergeant Ned Fletcher when they are called up to replace an infantry battalion that had suffered casualties at Dunkirk.

programme.title: Recon
programme.desc: In the final days of World War II, four American soldiers are sent on a reconnaissance mission led by an Italian partisan with indeterminate loyalties. Hunted by a mysterious sniper, they must fight to make it out alive. Directed by Robert David Port and stars Alexander Ludwig, Lochlyn Munro and Franco Nero.

programme.title: Barry Lyndon
programme.desc: Redmond Barry is a rogue Irishman who is forced to leave England when he mistakenly believes he has killed the fiancé of his paramour in a duel. Robbed of all his money, he enlists in the British army to fight in the Seven Years War in Europe. Eventually he deserts only to be discovered as a charlatan by the Prussian Captain Potzdorf, and forced to serve in the much harsher Prussian army. At the end of the war, the Prussian police minister gives Barry a position in the household of the Chevalier de Balibari, a conman and gambler, so that Barry can spy on him. Barry and the Chevalier get on famously, as both are Irish, and Barry becomes the pupil of the conman. In this company, Barry is admitted to the highest social circles in Europe. Directed by Stanley Kubrick and stars Ryan O'Neal, Marisa Berenson, Patrick Magee and Hardy Kruger.

programme.title: 2.6 Seconds: Death In The Outback
programme.desc: Episode 4 begins with the March 2022 acquittal of Constable Zachary Rolfe for the murder of Kumanjayi Walker, a verdict that sparks relief among Rolfe’s supporters and profound grief for Walker’s family and the Yuendumu community. While Rolfe describes the decision as the right outcome, family members say it reinforces their belief that justice has been denied. Determined to continue seeking answers, they turn their attention to the coronial inquest. The episode shifts beyond the criminal trial to examine broader questions about police conduct, accountability and institutional culture. Commencing in September 2022, the coronial inquest investigates events before, during and after the shooting, as well as evidence unavailable to the jury. It explores racist text messages found on Rolfe’s phone, previous incidents involving force against Aboriginal people and allegations of inappropriate conduct within the Northern Territory Police Force. The inquiry reveals evidence of racist language and behaviour among police officers, including offensive messages and the existence of Territory Response Group awards featuring racist imagery and terminology. These revelations expand scrutiny from Rolfe’s individual actions to the wider culture and leadership of the police organisation. Rolfe’s own testimony, delivered after lengthy legal challenges, further exposes concerns about accountability and institutional practices. In July 2025, Coroner Elisabeth Armitage delivers her findings in Yuendumu. While unable to determine criminal guilt, she concludes that Walker’s death was avoidable and describes the fatal arrest as a case of “officer-induced jeopardy.” The Coroner finds that police failures to adequately supervise and discipline Rolfe contributed to a culture of impunity. She also rejects Rolfe’s claim that Walker’s hand was on his firearm immediately before the first shot. The findings address racism directly, concluding that Rolfe was racist and that he operated within an organisation displaying hallmarks of institutional racism. The failure of officers to report racist Territory Response Group awards is cited as evidence of entrenched systemic problems within the Northern Territory Police Force. While police representatives acknowledge the findings and the need for reform, many Aboriginal contributors note that such concerns had been raised by communities for decades. The episode concludes with a mixture of recognition and frustration. Although the Coroner’s findings validate many concerns long expressed by Walker’s family, they do not deliver the accountability they sought. As family members continue to advocate for reform, community safety and justice, the series ends by remembering Kumanjayi Walker as a loved son, grandson, brother and cousin, while highlighting the unfinished work of addressing racism, police accountability and systemic change.

Directed by Stanley Kubrick and stars Ryan O'Neal, Marisa Berenson, Patrick Magee and Hardy Kruger.

programme.title: Cheese Slices
programme.sub-title: Twins Of The Mediterranean: Corsica And Sardinia
programme.desc: Despite being close neighbours, these two large islands in the Mediterranean have distinctly different cheese traditions. While sampling Corsica’s renowned Brocciu, a soft ewe’s milk cheese, Will is introduced to a traditional version ripened with maggots. After a short ferry ride and a drive into the beautiful mountains of Sardinia, he meets a rock star shepherd and discovers an ancient curd cheese matured in a goat’s stomach, before exploring authentic Pecorino Fiore Sardo, an exceptional cheese hand-made by shepherds then smoked over an open fire.

In this episode he catches up with a Hills Bee farmer to source a special honey for a crème brulee. Maggie’s journey into the hills takes her to a property called Nirvana. Yes, it’s heavenly, and so are the chestnuts she collects to make a delicious and surprisingly simple ravioli.

programme.desc: Sachie meets Kiwi entertainer and personality Lynda Topp. The two go to High Country Salmon for the catch a fish experience and to learn how the salmon is produced. They cook salmon on the banks of the lake.

programme.title: Marcus In The Med: Mallorca
programme.desc: Marcus has had an incredible time exploring the food of Mallorca and even though his journey is coming to an end there are still lots of classic dishes to discover, including cuarto and hot chocolate and Arroz Brut, a traditional rice dish which Marcus learns at a gathering of 4 generations of the same family.

programme.title: Feast By Fire
programme.desc: Jess explores the unexpected at Rossler's Blue Cord Barbecue, where raspberry burnt ends turn BBQ on its head. Inspired by the bold flavours, she creates her own version at home, guiding viewers through balancing sweetness and smoke for a dish that’s both playful and deeply satisfying.

programme.title: Thai Street Food: Best Kept Secrets
programme.desc: The world's strangest, yet most famous fruit, Michelin awarded fruit street snacks and a dessert that has made a Thai city famous, street food sellers uncover the endless and imaginative ways in which fruit is integrated into Thai life.

programme.title: Global Soul Kitchen
programme.desc: Chef Deborah VanTrece puts a soulful twist on the classic Polish dish Galumpkis by using smoked ham hocks.

programme.title: Remarkable Places To Eat
programme.desc: Pastry Chef Ravneet Gill takes Fred to Mallorca to experience incredible island cooking, from a buzzing beach bar serving holiday food in the sun, to light and fluffy pastries.

programme.title: Jamie's Easy Christmas Countdown
programme.desc: Jamie kicks off his easy Christmas countdown with a gorgeous smoked salmon pate that's elegant, luxurious, and can be rustled up in the time it takes to make some toast! A great little dish that works well as a Christmas Day starter, or a handy dip for any surprise guests.

programme.title: Rick Stein's Far Eastern Odyssey
programme.desc: In Sri Lanka, Rick Stein discovers a wealth of spicy vegetable curries. In Colombo, he meets one the country's most respected chefs and tastes an unforgettable chilli crab.

programme.title: Into The Kitchen
programme.desc: Alex Dilling changed the world is how a 2 Michelin star chef has described him. There was an explosion of the best dishes anyone had seen anywhere. The attention to detail and the precision in these dishes were incredible, and nearly all of his dishes went viral.

programme.title: Gary Barlow's Wine Tour: South Africa
programme.sub-title: Gary Barlow With Special Guest Eliot Kennedy
programme.desc: Gary begins his South African adventure, meeting his best friend and fellow musician Eliot Kennedy in Franschhoek.

programme.title: Eater's Guide To The World
programme.sub-title: Jungle To Table In Costa Rica
programme.desc: The Costa Rican jungle is basically nature's candy store and we'd like to invite you in. It's bursting with delicious guanabana, cainito, cas, pejibaye and cacao - known to some as the fruit of the Gods.

programme.title: 2.6 Seconds: Death In The Outback
programme.desc: Episode 4 begins with the March 2022 acquittal of Constable Zachary Rolfe for the murder of Kumanjayi Walker, a verdict that sparks relief among Rolfe’s supporters and profound grief for Walker’s family and the Yuendumu community. While Rolfe describes the decision as the right outcome, family members say it reinforces their belief that justice has been denied. Determined to continue seeking answers, they turn their attention to the coronial inquest. The episode shifts beyond the criminal trial to examine broader questions about police conduct, accountability and institutional culture. Commencing in September 2022, the coronial inquest investigates events before, during and after the shooting, as well as evidence unavailable to the jury. It explores racist text messages found on Rolfe’s phone, previous incidents involving force against Aboriginal people and allegations of inappropriate conduct within the Northern Territory Police Force. The inquiry reveals evidence of racist language and behaviour among police officers, including offensive messages and the existence of Territory Response Group awards featuring racist imagery and terminology. These revelations expand scrutiny from Rolfe’s individual actions to the wider culture and leadership of the police organisation. Rolfe’s own testimony, delivered after lengthy legal challenges, further exposes concerns about accountability and institutional practices. In July 2025, Coroner Elisabeth Armitage delivers her findings in Yuendumu. While unable to determine criminal guilt, she concludes that Walker’s death was avoidable and describes the fatal arrest as a case of “officer-induced jeopardy.” The Coroner finds that police failures to adequately supervise and discipline Rolfe contributed to a culture of impunity. She also rejects Rolfe’s claim that Walker’s hand was on his firearm immediately before the first shot. The findings address racism directly, concluding that Rolfe was racist and that he operated within an organisation displaying hallmarks of institutional racism. The failure of officers to report racist Territory Response Group awards is cited as evidence of entrenched systemic problems within the Northern Territory Police Force. While police representatives acknowledge the findings and the need for reform, many Aboriginal contributors note that such concerns had been raised by communities for decades. The episode concludes with a mixture of recognition and frustration. Although the Coroner’s findings validate many concerns long expressed by Walker’s family, they do not deliver the accountability they sought. As family members continue to advocate for reform, community safety and justice, the series ends by remembering Kumanjayi Walker as a loved son, grandson, brother and cousin, while highlighting the unfinished work of addressing racism, police accountability and systemic change.

programme.title: 2.6 Seconds: Death In The Outback
programme.desc: Episode 4 begins with the March 2022 acquittal of Constable Zachary Rolfe for the murder of Kumanjayi Walker, a verdict that sparks relief among Rolfe’s supporters and profound grief for Walker’s family and the Yuendumu community. While Rolfe describes the decision as the right outcome, family members say it reinforces their belief that justice has been denied. Determined to continue seeking answers, they turn their attention to the coronial inquest. The episode shifts beyond the criminal trial to examine broader questions about police conduct, accountability and institutional culture. Commencing in September 2022, the coronial inquest investigates events before, during and after the shooting, as well as evidence unavailable to the jury. It explores racist text messages found on Rolfe’s phone, previous incidents involving force against Aboriginal people and allegations of inappropriate conduct within the Northern Territory Police Force. The inquiry reveals evidence of racist language and behaviour among police officers, including offensive messages and the existence of Territory Response Group awards featuring racist imagery and terminology. These revelations expand scrutiny from Rolfe’s individual actions to the wider culture and leadership of the police organisation. Rolfe’s own testimony, delivered after lengthy legal challenges, further exposes concerns about accountability and institutional practices. In July 2025, Coroner Elisabeth Armitage delivers her findings in Yuendumu. While unable to determine criminal guilt, she concludes that Walker’s death was avoidable and describes the fatal arrest as a case of “officer-induced jeopardy.” The Coroner finds that police failures to adequately supervise and discipline Rolfe contributed to a culture of impunity. She also rejects Rolfe’s claim that Walker’s hand was on his firearm immediately before the first shot. The findings address racism directly, concluding that Rolfe was racist and that he operated within an organisation displaying hallmarks of institutional racism. The failure of officers to report racist Territory Response Group awards is cited as evidence of entrenched systemic problems within the Northern Territory Police Force. While police representatives acknowledge the findings and the need for reform, many Aboriginal contributors note that such concerns had been raised by communities for decades. The episode concludes with a mixture of recognition and frustration. Although the Coroner’s findings validate many concerns long expressed by Walker’s family, they do not deliver the accountability they sought. As family members continue to advocate for reform, community safety and justice, the series ends by remembering Kumanjayi Walker as a loved son, grandson, brother and cousin, while highlighting the unfinished work of addressing racism, police accountability and systemic change.

programme.desc: Redmond Barry is a rogue Irishman who is forced to leave England when he mistakenly believes he has killed the fiancé of his paramour in a duel. Robbed of all his money, he enlists in the British army to fight in the Seven Years War in Europe. Eventually he deserts only to be discovered as a charlatan by the Prussian Captain Potzdorf, and forced to serve in the much harsher Prussian army. At the end of the war, the Prussian police minister gives Barry a position in the household of the Chevalier de Balibari, a conman and gambler, so that Barry can spy on him. Barry and the Chevalier get on famously, as both are Irish, and Barry becomes the pupil of the conman. In this company, Barry is admitted to the highest social circles in Europe. Directed by Stanley Kubrick and stars Ryan O'Neal, Marisa Berenson, Patrick Magee and Hardy Kruger.

programme.title: Down With Love
programme.desc: When a ladies' man, man's man, man-about-town men's magazine journalist meets a popular pro-feminist author with a secret agenda of her own, a classic battle-of-the-sexes high jinx plot plays out to its expected happy "coupled" ending.

programme.title: La Chimera
programme.desc: An enchanting romantic adventure, an ethereal spiritual journey and a ripping heist movie like no other, La Chimera follows a young British archaeologist who gets caught up in an international network dealing in stolen Italian artefacts.

programme.title: The Way Ahead
programme.desc: A mismatched collection of conscripted civilians find training tough under Lieutenant Jim Perry and Sergeant Ned Fletcher when they are called up to replace an infantry battalion that had suffered casualties at Dunkirk.

programme.title: Time Bandits
programme.desc: Six fractious dwarfs steal a precious map that shows the locations of a series of time holes scattered across the universe, enabling them to travel back in time. Crashing through the bedroom wardrobe of 11 year old Craig Warnock and taking him along with them for the ride, they find themselves involved in a series of eccentric encounters with famous historical figures, amongst them Napoleon, Robin Hood and ancient Greece ruler, Agamemnon.

programme.title: Stay
programme.desc: A thriller about a psychologist whose client makes bizarre predictions that--to the psychologist's mounting terror-- begin to come true. He must race against time to save everything he loves before it disappears.

programme.title: Turn Me On
programme.desc: In a world where the inconvenience of human emotion has been eradicated by a single daily vitamin, one young couple skips their dose and discovers love, joy, sex and the baggage that comes with it.

programme.title: The Snows Of Kilimanjaro
programme.desc: The life of celebrated American writer Harry Street (Gregory Peck) flashes back before his eyes as he lies dying from a wound suffered at the foot of Tanzania's Mount Kilimanjaro. As he is tended to by his traveling companion, Helen (Susan Hayward), he recalls many things: his first wife and Paris literary inspiration, Cynthia Green (Ava Gardner) ; his second wife, Countess Liz (Hildegarde Neff) ; and his formative years with uncle Bill (Leo G. Carroll).

programme.title: Mary Shelley

But the real life story of Mary Shelley - and the creation of her immortal monster - is nearly as fantastical as her fiction. Directed by Haifaa Al-Mansour and stars Elle Fanning, Douglas Booth and Maisie Williams.

The story of William Wallace whose passion and courage united the Scottish people in the struggle against a ruthless English king over six hundred years ago, at the start of the fourteenth century.

He agrees to take part in a dangerous mission to save 123 Jewish orphans from the grasp of the Nazis and the ruthless Gestapo chief Klaus Barbie (Matthias Schweighöfer) and take them to safety across the border to Switzerland.

programme.title: 2.6 Seconds: Death In The Outback
programme.desc: Episode 4 begins with the March 2022 acquittal of Constable Zachary Rolfe for the murder of Kumanjayi Walker, a verdict that sparks relief among Rolfe’s supporters and profound grief for Walker’s family and the Yuendumu community. While Rolfe describes the decision as the right outcome, family members say it reinforces their belief that justice has been denied. Determined to continue seeking answers, they turn their attention to the coronial inquest. The episode shifts beyond the criminal trial to examine broader questions about police conduct, accountability and institutional culture. Commencing in September 2022, the coronial inquest investigates events before, during and after the shooting, as well as evidence unavailable to the jury. It explores racist text messages found on Rolfe’s phone, previous incidents involving force against Aboriginal people and allegations of inappropriate conduct within the Northern Territory Police Force. The inquiry reveals evidence of racist language and behaviour among police officers, including offensive messages and the existence of Territory Response Group awards featuring racist imagery and terminology. These revelations expand scrutiny from Rolfe’s individual actions to the wider culture and leadership of the police organisation. Rolfe’s own testimony, delivered after lengthy legal challenges, further exposes concerns about accountability and institutional practices. In July 2025, Coroner Elisabeth Armitage delivers her findings in Yuendumu. While unable to determine criminal guilt, she concludes that Walker’s death was avoidable and describes the fatal arrest as a case of “officer-induced jeopardy.” The Coroner finds that police failures to adequately supervise and discipline Rolfe contributed to a culture of impunity. She also rejects Rolfe’s claim that Walker’s hand was on his firearm immediately before the first shot. The findings address racism directly, concluding that Rolfe was racist and that he operated within an organisation displaying hallmarks of institutional racism. The failure of officers to report racist Territory Response Group awards is cited as evidence of entrenched systemic problems within the Northern Territory Police Force. While police representatives acknowledge the findings and the need for reform, many Aboriginal contributors note that such concerns had been raised by communities for decades. The episode concludes with a mixture of recognition and frustration. Although the Coroner’s findings validate many concerns long expressed by Walker’s family, they do not deliver the accountability they sought. As family members continue to advocate for reform, community safety and justice, the series ends by remembering Kumanjayi Walker as a loved son, grandson, brother and cousin, while highlighting the unfinished work of addressing racism, police accountability and systemic change.

A compelling tale of geopolitical tension, diplomacy and the quest for power.

programme.title: Royals And Their Gardens

Later a royal retreat under Charles II and a WWII spy base, the estate has seen royal drama, financial ruin, and espionage. Today, with gardens by Capability Brown and interiors by Robert Adam, it stands as a grand relic of England's aristocratic legacy.

programme.title: The Three Kings Of 1936
programme.desc: Narrated by Tracy-Ann Oberman, The Three Kings of 1936 explores a pivotal year in royal history. Through rare archive material, expert analysis and eyewitness accounts, it traces the death of George V, the abdication of Edward VIII and the accession of George VI. Set against a backdrop of social change and political turmoil, it reveals how these events reshaped the monarchy.

Featuring stunning original performances by some of the greatest dance practitioners and a wealth of archive materials.

Directed by Stanley Kubrick and stars Ryan O'Neal, Marisa Berenson, Patrick Magee and Hardy Kruger.

programme.desc: Marcus has had an incredible time exploring the food of Mallorca and even though his journey is coming to an end there are still lots of classic dishes to discover, including cuarto and hot chocolate and Arroz Brut, a traditional rice dish which Marcus learns at a gathering of 4 generations of the same family.

programme.title: Feast By Fire
programme.desc: Jess explores the unexpected at Rossler's Blue Cord Barbecue, where raspberry burnt ends turn BBQ on its head. Inspired by the bold flavours, she creates her own version at home, guiding viewers through balancing sweetness and smoke for a dish that’s both playful and deeply satisfying.

programme.title: Thai Street Food: Best Kept Secrets
programme.desc: The world's strangest, yet most famous fruit, Michelin awarded fruit street snacks and a dessert that has made a Thai city famous, street food sellers uncover the endless and imaginative ways in which fruit is integrated into Thai life.

programme.title: Global Soul Kitchen

programme.title: Remarkable Places To Eat

programme.title: Jamie's Easy Christmas Countdown
programme.desc: Jamie kicks off his easy Christmas countdown with a gorgeous smoked salmon pate that's elegant, luxurious, and can be rustled up in the time it takes to make some toast! A great little dish that works well as a Christmas Day starter, or a handy dip for any surprise guests.

programme.title: Rick Stein's Far Eastern Odyssey
programme.desc: In Sri Lanka, Rick Stein discovers a wealth of spicy vegetable curries. In Colombo, he meets one the country's most respected chefs and tastes an unforgettable chilli crab.

programme.title: Into The Kitchen
programme.desc: Alex Dilling changed the world is how a 2 Michelin star chef has described him. There was an explosion of the best dishes anyone had seen anywhere. The attention to detail and the precision in these dishes were incredible, and nearly all of his dishes went viral.

programme.desc: Gary begins his South African adventure, meeting his best friend and fellow musician Eliot Kennedy in Franschhoek.

programme.sub-title: Jungle To Table In Costa Rica
programme.desc: The Costa Rican jungle is basically nature's candy store and we'd like to invite you in. It's bursting with delicious guanabana, cainito, cas, pejibaye and cacao - known to some as the fruit of the Gods.

programme.title: Those Who Stayed
programme.desc: Olga, her two kids and two husbands, one of whom is an ex-, have to live together in a tiny one-room apartment. They try hard to survive and not to kill each other in the process.

programme.title: Those Who Stayed
programme.desc: Max is a zookeeper at the private zoo. He is not a fan of his job, and February 24th is supposed to be his last day. But the Russians surround the area and blow up the bridge. The zoo is left without electricity and food, and the animals are on the verge of death. Max wants to go and get food, but his evacuation plan turns into a suicide mission.

programme.title: Those Who Stayed
programme.desc: Yura is homeless living in the car with his 10-year-old son after fleeing from the war. When the fighting had caught up to him, he decides to stand his ground.

programme.title: Those Who Stayed
programme.desc: Klaus is a young German surgeon. When the war starts, he drives to Kyiv to whisk away his Ukrainian girlfriend. But she refuses to flee, so Hans also stays, inspired by the volunteer movement, until one day he finds himself heavily-wounded.

programme.title: Those Who Stayed
programme.desc: Egor lives with his two mothers, one of whom is a surgeon at the children's hospital. Every time the sirens announce air raids, He puts on his bike helmet and hides in the bathroom. He is fighting with rockets, bombs and his own fears with the help of his imaginary friends - animated birds from a tablet's game.

programme.title: Those Who Stayed
programme.desc: A world famous singer, known as his drag persona Verka Serduchka, does not run or hide from the war. He stays home alone without assistants, servants or security in the very centre of Kyiv. He streams every day and becomes the public symbol of Ukrainian resistance.

programme.title: 2.6 Seconds: Death In The Outback
programme.desc: Episode 4 begins with the March 2022 acquittal of Constable Zachary Rolfe for the murder of Kumanjayi Walker, a verdict that sparks relief among Rolfe’s supporters and profound grief for Walker’s family and the Yuendumu community. While Rolfe describes the decision as the right outcome, family members say it reinforces their belief that justice has been denied. Determined to continue seeking answers, they turn their attention to the coronial inquest. The episode shifts beyond the criminal trial to examine broader questions about police conduct, accountability and institutional culture. Commencing in September 2022, the coronial inquest investigates events before, during and after the shooting, as well as evidence unavailable to the jury. It explores racist text messages found on Rolfe’s phone, previous incidents involving force against Aboriginal people and allegations of inappropriate conduct within the Northern Territory Police Force. The inquiry reveals evidence of racist language and behaviour among police officers, including offensive messages and the existence of Territory Response Group awards featuring racist imagery and terminology. These revelations expand scrutiny from Rolfe’s individual actions to the wider culture and leadership of the police organisation. Rolfe’s own testimony, delivered after lengthy legal challenges, further exposes concerns about accountability and institutional practices. In July 2025, Coroner Elisabeth Armitage delivers her findings in Yuendumu. While unable to determine criminal guilt, she concludes that Walker’s death was avoidable and describes the fatal arrest as a case of “officer-induced jeopardy.” The Coroner finds that police failures to adequately supervise and discipline Rolfe contributed to a culture of impunity. She also rejects Rolfe’s claim that Walker’s hand was on his firearm immediately before the first shot. The findings address racism directly, concluding that Rolfe was racist and that he operated within an organisation displaying hallmarks of institutional racism. The failure of officers to report racist Territory Response Group awards is cited as evidence of entrenched systemic problems within the Northern Territory Police Force. While police representatives acknowledge the findings and the need for reform, many Aboriginal contributors note that such concerns had been raised by communities for decades. The episode concludes with a mixture of recognition and frustration. Although the Coroner’s findings validate many concerns long expressed by Walker’s family, they do not deliver the accountability they sought. As family members continue to advocate for reform, community safety and justice, the series ends by remembering Kumanjayi Walker as a loved son, grandson, brother and cousin, while highlighting the unfinished work of addressing racism, police accountability and systemic change.

programme.title: 2.6 Seconds: Death In The Outback
programme.desc: Episode 4 begins with the March 2022 acquittal of Constable Zachary Rolfe for the murder of Kumanjayi Walker, a verdict that sparks relief among Rolfe’s supporters and profound grief for Walker’s family and the Yuendumu community. While Rolfe describes the decision as the right outcome, family members say it reinforces their belief that justice has been denied. Determined to continue seeking answers, they turn their attention to the coronial inquest. The episode shifts beyond the criminal trial to examine broader questions about police conduct, accountability and institutional culture. Commencing in September 2022, the coronial inquest investigates events before, during and after the shooting, as well as evidence unavailable to the jury. It explores racist text messages found on Rolfe’s phone, previous incidents involving force against Aboriginal people and allegations of inappropriate conduct within the Northern Territory Police Force. The inquiry reveals evidence of racist language and behaviour among police officers, including offensive messages and the existence of Territory Response Group awards featuring racist imagery and terminology. These revelations expand scrutiny from Rolfe’s individual actions to the wider culture and leadership of the police organisation. Rolfe’s own testimony, delivered after lengthy legal challenges, further exposes concerns about accountability and institutional practices. In July 2025, Coroner Elisabeth Armitage delivers her findings in Yuendumu. While unable to determine criminal guilt, she concludes that Walker’s death was avoidable and describes the fatal arrest as a case of “officer-induced jeopardy.” The Coroner finds that police failures to adequately supervise and discipline Rolfe contributed to a culture of impunity. She also rejects Rolfe’s claim that Walker’s hand was on his firearm immediately before the first shot. The findings address racism directly, concluding that Rolfe was racist and that he operated within an organisation displaying hallmarks of institutional racism. The failure of officers to report racist Territory Response Group awards is cited as evidence of entrenched systemic problems within the Northern Territory Police Force. While police representatives acknowledge the findings and the need for reform, many Aboriginal contributors note that such concerns had been raised by communities for decades. The episode concludes with a mixture of recognition and frustration. Although the Coroner’s findings validate many concerns long expressed by Walker’s family, they do not deliver the accountability they sought. As family members continue to advocate for reform, community safety and justice, the series ends by remembering Kumanjayi Walker as a loved son, grandson, brother and cousin, while highlighting the unfinished work of addressing racism, police accountability and systemic change.

programme.desc: An enchanting romantic adventure, an ethereal spiritual journey and a ripping heist movie like no other, La Chimera follows a young British archaeologist who gets caught up in an international network dealing in stolen Italian artefacts.

programme.title: The Way Ahead
programme.desc: A mismatched collection of conscripted civilians find training tough under Lieutenant Jim Perry and Sergeant Ned Fletcher when they are called up to replace an infantry battalion that had suffered casualties at Dunkirk.

programme.title: Time Bandits
programme.desc: Six fractious dwarfs steal a precious map that shows the locations of a series of time holes scattered across the universe, enabling them to travel back in time. programme.title: Stay
programme.desc: A thriller about a psychologist whose client makes bizarre predictions that--to the psychologist's mounting terror-- begin to come true. He must race against time to save everything he loves before it disappears.

programme.title: Turn Me On
programme.desc: In a world where the inconvenience of human emotion has been eradicated by a single daily vitamin, one young couple skips their dose and discovers love, joy, sex and the baggage that comes with it.

programme.title: The Snows Of Kilimanjaro

As he is tended to by his traveling companion, Helen (Susan Hayward), he recalls many things: his first wife and Paris literary inspiration, Cynthia Green (Ava Gardner) ; his second wife, Countess Liz (Hildegarde Neff) ; and his formative years with uncle Bill (Leo G. Carroll).

programme.title: Mary Shelley

But the real life story of Mary Shelley - and the creation of her immortal monster - is nearly as fantastical as her fiction. Directed by Haifaa Al-Mansour and stars Elle Fanning, Douglas Booth and Maisie Williams.

programme.title: Living
programme.desc: In 1950s London, a humourless bureaucrat decides to take time off work to experience life after receiving a grim diagnosis.

programme.title: Braveheart

The story of William Wallace whose passion and courage united the Scottish people in the struggle against a ruthless English king over six hundred years ago, at the start of the fourteenth century.

programme.title: Resistance
programme.desc: Before he becomes known as the world-famous mime Marcel Marceau, aspiring Jewish actor Marcel Mangel (Jesse Eisenberg) joins the French Resistance during the war. He agrees to take part in a dangerous mission to save 123 Jewish orphans from the grasp of the Nazis and the ruthless Gestapo chief Klaus Barbie (Matthias Schweighöfer) and take them to safety across the border to Switzerland.

programme.title: 2.6 Seconds: Death In The Outback
programme.desc: Episode 4 begins with the March 2022 acquittal of Constable Zachary Rolfe for the murder of Kumanjayi Walker, a verdict that sparks relief among Rolfe’s supporters and profound grief for Walker’s family and the Yuendumu community. While Rolfe describes the decision as the right outcome, family members say it reinforces their belief that justice has been denied. Determined to continue seeking answers, they turn their attention to the coronial inquest. The episode shifts beyond the criminal trial to examine broader questions about police conduct, accountability and institutional culture. Commencing in September 2022, the coronial inquest investigates events before, during and after the shooting, as well as evidence unavailable to the jury. It explores racist text messages found on Rolfe’s phone, previous incidents involving force against Aboriginal people and allegations of inappropriate conduct within the Northern Territory Police Force. The inquiry reveals evidence of racist language and behaviour among police officers, including offensive messages and the existence of Territory Response Group awards featuring racist imagery and terminology. These revelations expand scrutiny from Rolfe’s individual actions to the wider culture and leadership of the police organisation. Rolfe’s own testimony, delivered after lengthy legal challenges, further exposes concerns about accountability and institutional practices. In July 2025, Coroner Elisabeth Armitage delivers her findings in Yuendumu. While unable to determine criminal guilt, she concludes that Walker’s death was avoidable and describes the fatal arrest as a case of “officer-induced jeopardy.” The Coroner finds that police failures to adequately supervise and discipline Rolfe contributed to a culture of impunity. She also rejects Rolfe’s claim that Walker’s hand was on his firearm immediately before the first shot. The findings address racism directly, concluding that Rolfe was racist and that he operated within an organisation displaying hallmarks of institutional racism. The failure of officers to report racist Territory Response Group awards is cited as evidence of entrenched systemic problems within the Northern Territory Police Force. While police representatives acknowledge the findings and the need for reform, many Aboriginal contributors note that such concerns had been raised by communities for decades. The episode concludes with a mixture of recognition and frustration. Although the Coroner’s findings validate many concerns long expressed by Walker’s family, they do not deliver the accountability they sought. As family members continue to advocate for reform, community safety and justice, the series ends by remembering Kumanjayi Walker as a loved son, grandson, brother and cousin, while highlighting the unfinished work of addressing racism, police accountability and systemic change.

Carroll).

Directed by Ben Cookson and stars Noah Schnapp, Jean Reno and Anjelica Huston.

programme.title: Barry Lyndon
programme.desc: Redmond Barry is a rogue Irishman who is forced to leave England when he mistakenly believes he has killed the fiancé of his paramour in a duel. Robbed of all his money, he enlists in the British army to fight in the Seven Years War in Europe. Eventually he deserts only to be discovered as a charlatan by the Prussian Captain Potzdorf, and forced to serve in the much harsher Prussian army. At the end of the war, the Prussian police minister gives Barry a position in the household of the Chevalier de Balibari, a conman and gambler, so that Barry can spy on him. Barry and the Chevalier get on famously, as both are Irish, and Barry becomes the pupil of the conman. In this company, Barry is admitted to the highest social circles in Europe. Directed by Stanley Kubrick and stars Ryan O'Neal, Marisa Berenson, Patrick Magee and Hardy Kruger.

programme.title: 2.6 Seconds: Death In The Outback
programme.desc: Episode 4 begins with the March 2022 acquittal of Constable Zachary Rolfe for the murder of Kumanjayi Walker, a verdict that sparks relief among Rolfe’s supporters and profound grief for Walker’s family and the Yuendumu community. While Rolfe describes the decision as the right outcome, family members say it reinforces their belief that justice has been denied. Determined to continue seeking answers, they turn their attention to the coronial inquest. The episode shifts beyond the criminal trial to examine broader questions about police conduct, accountability and institutional culture. Commencing in September 2022, the coronial inquest investigates events before, during and after the shooting, as well as evidence unavailable to the jury. It explores racist text messages found on Rolfe’s phone, previous incidents involving force against Aboriginal people and allegations of inappropriate conduct within the Northern Territory Police Force. The inquiry reveals evidence of racist language and behaviour among police officers, including offensive messages and the existence of Territory Response Group awards featuring racist imagery and terminology. These revelations expand scrutiny from Rolfe’s individual actions to the wider culture and leadership of the police organisation. Rolfe’s own testimony, delivered after lengthy legal challenges, further exposes concerns about accountability and institutional practices. In July 2025, Coroner Elisabeth Armitage delivers her findings in Yuendumu. While unable to determine criminal guilt, she concludes that Walker’s death was avoidable and describes the fatal arrest as a case of “officer-induced jeopardy.” The Coroner finds that police failures to adequately supervise and discipline Rolfe contributed to a culture of impunity. She also rejects Rolfe’s claim that Walker’s hand was on his firearm immediately before the first shot. The findings address racism directly, concluding that Rolfe was racist and that he operated within an organisation displaying hallmarks of institutional racism. The failure of officers to report racist Territory Response Group awards is cited as evidence of entrenched systemic problems within the Northern Territory Police Force. While police representatives acknowledge the findings and the need for reform, many Aboriginal contributors note that such concerns had been raised by communities for decades. The episode concludes with a mixture of recognition and frustration. Although the Coroner’s findings validate many concerns long expressed by Walker’s family, they do not deliver the accountability they sought. As family members continue to advocate for reform, community safety and justice, the series ends by remembering Kumanjayi Walker as a loved son, grandson, brother and cousin, while highlighting the unfinished work of addressing racism, police accountability and systemic change.
